children.title: Uniformly Bounded Set Families
children.top_down_role: Families controlled by a common bounded region.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathscr A\) is a family of nonempty subsets of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathscr A\) is uniformly bounded exactly when one common bounded ball contains every member.

notation.meaning: Closed ball centered at x with radius R.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform boundedness with a common center and radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(\mathscr A\) is uniformly bounded if there exist \(x_0\in X\) and \(R<\infty\) such that \[A\subseteq\overline B(x_0,R)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\mathscr A.\] Equivalently, for some \(x_0\in X\), \[\sup_{A\in\mathscr A}\sup_{a\in A}d(a,x_0)<\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set family is uniformly bounded when all its members lie in one common bounded ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Bounded Set Families

children.title: Hausdorff Precompactness
children.top_down_role: Precompactness consequences under bounded compact-set regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathscr A\) is relatively compact in \(d_H\) if and only if it is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Hausdorff precompactness criterion for nonempty compact sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\mathscr A\subset\mathcal K(\mathbb R^m)\) is relatively compact for the Hausdorff metric if and only if there exists \(R<\infty\) such that \[A\subseteq\overline B(0,R)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\mathscr A.\] Thus every sequence in a uniformly bounded family has a Hausdorff-convergent subsequence whose limit is nonempty and compact; conversely, every Hausdorff-relatively-compact family is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, a family of nonempty compact sets is Hausdorff precompact exactly when it is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Hausdorff Precompactness

children.title: Locally Compact Set Families
children.top_down_role: Set families with compact behavior on bounded regions.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F(X)\) denotes all closed subsets of \(X\), including the empty set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sequence in \(\mathcal F(X)\) has a subsequence converging locally on compact observation windows.

notation.meaning: All closed subsets of X, including the empty set.
Closed ball centered at a fixed base point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential local compactness of closed-set families in a proper metric space.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108; H.* Metric Descriptions of Convergence p. 181

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every sequence \((F_n)\subset\mathcal F(X)\), properness of \(X\) permits successive Hausdorff subsequence extraction on the compact balls \(B_1,B_2,\ldots\). A diagonal subsequence has compatible limits on all bounded observation windows and therefore converges to a closed set \(F\in\mathcal F(X)\) in the local, Fell, or Attouch--Wets hyperspace topology. The limit may be empty when all members eventually leave each bounded region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed subsets of a proper metric space admit locally convergent subsequences, although the resulting closed limit may be empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Locally Compact Set Families

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108; H.* Metric Descriptions of Convergence p. 181

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The candidate conflates local convergence, Fell convergence, and an Attouch--Wets hyperspace topology while including the empty set, although the usual distance-function formulation of the Attouch--Wets topology requires additional conventions for the empty set. The cited locator does not establish this proper-metric-space formulation or the asserted equivalence of all three topologies. A source and precise topology definition are required before the mathematical statement can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Unbounded Set Families
children.top_down_role: Families whose members or union escape every bounded region.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathscr A\) is a family of nonempty subsets of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathscr A\) is unbounded exactly when no bounded ball contains all its members.

notation.meaning: Distance from the reference point to x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negation of uniform boundedness for a set family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(\mathscr A\) is unbounded if it is not uniformly bounded. Equivalently, for every \(x_0\in X\) and every \(R<\infty\), there exist \(A\in\mathscr A\) and \(a\in A\) such that \(d(a,x_0)>R\). Thus \[\sup_{A\in\mathscr A}\sup_{a\in A}d(a,x_0)=\infty\] for one, and hence every, reference point \(x_0\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is unbounded when points from its members occur arbitrarily far from every fixed reference point.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Set Families

children.title: Local Compactness Framework
children.top_down_role: Localization of compactness arguments for unbounded families.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a locally compact Hausdorff space with a countable base.
\(\mathcal F(X)\) contains all closed subsets, including \(\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(X)\) is compact and metrizable in the Fell topology.

notation.meaning: Hyperspace of all closed subsets of X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fell hyperspace compactness for second-countable locally compact Hausdorff spaces.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108; H.* Metric Descriptions of Convergence p. 181

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equip \(\mathcal F(X)\) with the Fell topology generated by the hit sets \(\{F:F\cap U\neq\varnothing\}\) for open \(U\subseteq X\) and the miss sets \(\{F:F\cap K=\varnothing\}\) for compact \(K\subseteq X\). Then \((\mathcal F(X),\tau_F)\) is compact and metrizable. Inclusion of \(\varnothing\) is essential for compactness because sequences of nonempty closed sets may escape every compact subset of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed-set hyperspace of a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space is compact and metrizable in the Fell topology when the empty set is included.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Compactness Framework

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108; H.* Metric Descriptions of Convergence p. 181

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Fell-hyperspace theorem is standard under suitable locally compact, second-countable Hausdorff hypotheses, but the cited variational-analysis chapter locator does not inspectably support this general topological hyperspace result. A specific Fell-topology theorem or hyperspace reference is required for the stated generality.

children.title: Escape to Infinity
children.top_down_role: Set mass or components leaving every bounded region.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a proper metric space with base point \(x_0\).
\(F_n\subseteq X\) is nonempty and closed for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(d(x_0,F_n)\to\infty\), then \(F_n\to\varnothing\) in the Fell topology.

notation.meaning: Distance from the base point to the set.
Closed ball centered at the base point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empty-limit mechanism caused by recession beyond every bounded observation window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \[d(x_0,F_n)\longrightarrow\infty,\] then for every \(R<\infty\) there exists \(N_R\) such that \[F_n\cap B_R(x_0)=\varnothing\qquad\text{for every }n\geq N_R.\] Consequently, \(F_n\to\varnothing\) in the Fell topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonempty closed sets have empty Fell limit when their distance from a fixed base point tends to infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape to Infinity

children.title: Local Vanishing
children.top_down_role: Disappearance of sets within each fixed bounded region.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local vanishing means \(F_n\cap K=\varnothing\) eventually for every compact \(K\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-window criterion for disappearance of a closed-set sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((F_n)\) vanishes locally if \[\text{for every compact }K\subseteq X\text{ there exists }N_K\text{ such that }F_n\cap K=\varnothing\text{ for all }n\geq N_K.\] In a proper metric space this is equivalent to eventual emptiness on every closed bounded ball. For nonempty \(F_n\), it is also equivalent to \(d(x_0,F_n)\to\infty\) for any fixed base point \(x_0\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local vanishing means that every compact observation region is eventually disjoint from the closed sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Vanishing

children.title: Empty-Limit Formation
children.top_down_role: Formation of an empty limiting set.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a locally compact Hausdorff space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n\to\varnothing\) in the Fell topology if and only if every compact subset is eventually missed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of convergence to the empty set in the Fell topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((F_n)\) converges to \(\varnothing\) in the Fell topology precisely when \[\forall K\subseteq X\text{ compact},\quad \exists N_K\quad \forall n\geq N_K,\quad F_n\cap K=\varnothing.\] The usual hit condition is vacuous for the empty limit, while the displayed compact-miss condition is exactly the remaining Fell convergence requirement. Thus empty-limit formation is the hyperspace manifestation of local vanishing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed-set sequence has empty Fell limit exactly when it eventually misses every compact subset of the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Limit Formation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The characterization of convergence to the empty set in the Fell topology is mathematically standard, but the cited variational-analysis chapter does not inspectably support the stated locally compact Hausdorff generality. A specific Fell-topology section or theorem is required; the proof-style explanatory sentences should also be removed when the sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Nonempty-Limit Recovery
children.top_down_role: Conditions preventing complete loss of limiting points.

assumptions_latex: \(F_n\subseteq X\) is nonempty and closed for every \(n\).
There exist \(x_n\in F_n\) contained in one bounded subset of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Some subsequence of \((F_n)\) has a nonempty Fell limit.

notation.meaning: Selected anchor point in the nth set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-anchor condition preventing an empty subsequential limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose there are \(x_0\in X\), \(R<\infty\), and points \(x_n\in F_n\) such that \[x_n\in B_R(x_0)\qquad\text{for every }n.\] Then some subsequence \((F_{n_j})\) converges in the Fell topology to a nonempty closed set \(F\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded choice of one anchor point from each closed set guarantees a subsequence with a nonempty Fell limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonempty-Limit Recovery

assumptions_latex: Each \(C_n\subset X\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is closed and convex, with the empty set allowed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence, allowing an empty limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For closed convex sets \(C_n\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), if \[\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}C_n=\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}C_n=C,\] then \(C\) is closed and convex. The conclusion permits \(C=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Painlevé–Kuratowski limit of closed convex subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is closed and convex; the limit may be empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Set Convergence

children.title: Cone Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes specialized to cones.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_n\to K\) exactly when its Painlevé--Kuratowski inner and outer limits both equal \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence specialized to closed cones in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence of closed cones \(K_n\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) converges to a closed cone \(K\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense when \[\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}K_n=\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}K_n=K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone convergence is Painlevé–Kuratowski set convergence restricted to closed cones: the outer and inner limits must both equal the limiting cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Convergence

children.title: Polar-Cone Limits
children.top_down_role: Limiting behavior of polar cones.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_n^\circ\to K^\circ\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity of negative polarity for closed convex cones in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cone \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), define its negative polar by \[K^\circ=\bigl\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:\langle y,x\rangle\leq0\text{ for every }x\in K\bigr\}.\] If closed convex cones \(K_n\) converge in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense to a closed convex cone \(K\), then \[\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}K_n^\circ=\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}K_n^\circ=K^\circ.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed convex cones in finite dimensions, taking the negative polar commutes with Painlevé–Kuratowski limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Cone Limits

children.title: Polarity Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of polarity with cone limits.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_n\to K\iff K_n^\circ\to K^\circ\), and \(K^{\circ\circ}=K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-convex polarity as an involutive convergence duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every closed convex cone \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), negative polarity is involutive: \[K^{\circ\circ}=K.\] For closed convex cones \(K_n,K\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), \[K_n\to K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K_n^\circ\to K^\circ,\] where both convergences are Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On closed convex cones, negative polarity is involutive, and convergence of cones is equivalent to convergence of their negative polar cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Polarity Compatibility

children.title: Duality Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where limiting operations fail to preserve polar duality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(C_n\to C\), one has \(C_n^\circ\not\to C^\circ\).

notation.meaning: nonconic singleton sequence and its limit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure after removing the cone hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb{R}\), let \(C_n=\{1/n\}\) and \(C=\{0\}\). Then \(C_n\to C\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense, whereas \[C_n^\circ=(-\infty,0]\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad C^\circ=\mathbb{R}.\] Consequently, \(C_n^\circ\to(-\infty,0]\neq C^\circ\). Thus polarity compatibility can fail when the cone hypothesis is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity need not commute with set limits outside the cone class: positive singletons converge to zero, while their polars do not converge to the polar of zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality Failure Boundary

children.title: Horizon-Recession Limit Pair
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic set behavior carried by directions escaping bounded regions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Horizon-cone convergence means \(C_n^\infty\to C^\infty\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional horizon cones and their Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), its horizon cone is \[C^\infty=\bigl\{w\in\mathbb{R}^d:\text{there exist }x_k\in C\text{ and }t_k\downarrow0\text{ with }t_kx_k\to w\bigr\}.\] The horizon cones of \(C_n\) converge to the horizon cone of \(C\) when \[\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}C_n^\infty=\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}C_n^\infty=C^\infty.\] For closed convex \(C\), the horizon cone equals the recession cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Horizon-cone convergence requires the horizon cones of the sets to converge in the Painlevé–Kuratowski sense to the horizon cone of the limiting set.
knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Cone Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(C_n	o C\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is recession-sensitive precisely when \(C_n^\infty	o C^\infty\).

notation.meaning: horizon cone, equal to the recession cone for closed convex sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set convergence augmented by exact convergence of asymptotic directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convergent sequence \(C_n	o C\) lies in a recession-sensitive stable regime when its ordinary set limit and its asymptotic-direction limit are simultaneously exact:
\[
\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n	o\infty}C_n^\infty
=
\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n	o\infty}C_n^\infty
=C^\infty.
\]
The outer equality excludes asymptotic directions persisting along subsequences without belonging to \(C^\infty\); the inner equality requires every direction in \(C^\infty\) to be approximable by directions from all sufficiently late \(C_n^\infty\). For closed convex sets, the same condition can be written using recession cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recession-sensitive stable regime combines ordinary set convergence with exact convergence of horizon, or convex recession, cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Sensitive Limit Regimes

children.title: Loss of Asymptotic Directions
children.top_down_role: Disappearance of previously present directions in the limit.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_n\to\{0\}\), but \(C_n^\infty=[0,\infty)\) while \(\{0\}^\infty=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: closed set with an escaping unbounded component

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex escaping-component example of lost horizon directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \[C_n=\{0\}\cup[n,\infty)\subset\mathbb{R}.\] Then \(C_n\to\{0\}\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense, but \[C_n^\infty=[0,\infty)\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad \bigl(\{0\}\bigr)^\infty=\{0\}.\] Thus the positive asymptotic directions of the escaping unbounded component are absent from the limit set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded component can escape while the sets converge, causing all of its positive horizon directions to disappear from the limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Asymptotic Directions

children.title: Creation of Asymptotic Directions
children.top_down_role: Appearance of new directions only at the limit.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_n\to[0,\infty)\), but \(C_n^\infty=\{0\}\) while \([0,\infty)^\infty=[0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expanding compact convex sets create a limiting recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(C_n=[0,n]\subset\mathbb{R}\). Then \[C_n\to C=[0,\infty)\] in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense. Moreover, \[C_n^\infty=\{0\}\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad C^\infty=[0,\infty).\] Hence \[\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}C_n^\infty=\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}C_n^\infty=\{0\}\neq C^\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding compact intervals converge to a ray, creating positive asymptotic directions absent from every approximating horizon cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Creation of Asymptotic Directions

children.title: Asymptotic-Direction Stability
children.top_down_role: Regimes preserving directional behavior through set convergence.

assumptions_latex: \(C_n	o C\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Asymptotic directions are stable iff \(\operatorname*{Limsup}_n C_n^\infty=\operatorname*{Liminf}_n C_n^\infty=C^\infty\).

notation.meaning: distance from a point to a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion excluding both loss and creation of horizon directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Asymptotic directions are stable along \(C_n	o C\) precisely when
\[
\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n	o\infty}C_n^\infty
=
\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n	o\infty}C_n^\infty
=C^\infty.
\]
Equivalently, every convergent subsequence \(w_{n_k}	o w\) with \(w_{n_k}\in C_{n_k}^\infty\) satisfies \(w\in C^\infty\), and every \(w\in C^\infty\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(w,C_n^\infty)	o0\). The first requirement prevents persistent directions from being lost; the second prevents directions from appearing only after passage to the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asymptotic-direction stability holds exactly when outer exclusion and inner recovery make the horizon cones converge to the limit set’s horizon cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic-Direction Stability

children.title: Operations on Convergent Sets
children.top_down_role: Preservation and failure of set convergence under algebraic and transformational constructions.

children.title: Finite Union Stability
children.top_down_role: Limit preservation for finite unions.

assumptions_latex: For every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(A_n^j\to A^j\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{j=1}^m A_n^j\to\bigcup_{j=1}^m A^j\).

notation.meaning: finite union at index n and its limit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions under Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) be fixed. If \(A_n^j\to A^j\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), then \[\bigcup_{j=1}^m A_n^j\to\bigcup_{j=1}^m A^j\] in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed finite index set, the union of componentwise convergent set sequences converges to the union of the component limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Union Stability

children.title: Infinite Union Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Instability introduced by unrestricted or nonuniform unions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every fixed \(j\), \(A_n^j\to\{0\}\), but \(\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}A_n^j=\{0,1\}\not\to\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}\{0\}=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal counterexample showing failure for countably infinite unions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n,j\in\mathbb{N}\), define \[A_n^j=\begin{cases}\{1\},&j=n,\\\{0\},&j\neq n.\end{cases}\] For every fixed \(j\), \(A_n^j\to A^j=\{0\}\). However, \[\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}A_n^j=\{0,1\}\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}A^j=\{0\}.\] Thus componentwise convergence of a countably infinite family does not ensure convergence of the corresponding unions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Countably infinite unions are unstable under componentwise set convergence because a moving diagonal component can survive in every union.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Union Failure Boundary

children.title: Cartesian Product Stability
children.top_down_role: Limit preservation for Cartesian products of varying sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Product Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Painlevé--Kuratowski product rule, including empty limiting factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_n,A\subset\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(B_n,B\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) be closed. If \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense, then
\[
A_n\times B_n\to A\times B.
\]
The assertion also applies when either limiting factor is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Painlevé–Kuratowski convergence of two set sequences implies convergence of their Cartesian products, including when a limiting factor is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_n\times B_n\to A\times B\).

children.title: Intersection Stability
children.top_down_role: Preservation of set limits under intersections.

assumptions_latex: \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\) are closed-set convergences in \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
Near every \(z\in A\cap B\), eventually \(d(x,A_n\cap B_n)\leq\kappa[d(x,A_n)+d(x,B_n)]\) for one local constant \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_n\cap B_n\to A\cap B\).

notation.meaning: distance from a point to a set, with distance to the empty set infinite

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient intersection rule under a uniform local linear-regularity estimate.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Sequential Normal Compactness of Set Intersections and Inverse Images p. 341
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_n,B_n,A,B\) be closed subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^d\), with \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\). Suppose that for every \(z\in A\cap B\) there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(z\), \(\kappa>0\), and \(n_0\) such that, for \(n\geq n_0\) and \(x\in U\),
\[
d(x,A_n\cap B_n)\leq\kappa\bigl(d(x,A_n)+d(x,B_n)\bigr).
\]
Then \(A_n\cap B_n\to A\cap B\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersections converge when the individual sets converge and a uniform local error bound prevents their approximating intersections from separating.
knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Stability

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Sequential Normal Compactness of Set Intersections and Inverse Images p. 341
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

children.title: Constraint Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions among varying constraint families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_n\cap B_n=\{x:(x,x)\in A_n\times B_n\}=\delta^{-1}(A_n\times B_n)\), where \(\delta(x)=(x,x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection constraints represented as product constraints coupled through the diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For closed sets \(A_n,B_n\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), define the diagonal embedding \(\delta:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^{2d}\) by \(\delta(x)=(x,x)\) and the diagonal \(\Delta=\delta(\mathbb{R}^d)\). Then
\[
A_n\cap B_n=\delta^{-1}(A_n\times B_n),
\]
and, equivalently,
\[
\delta(A_n\cap B_n)=(A_n\times B_n)\cap\Delta.
\]
Thus stability of intersections is precisely stability of an inverse-image constraint, or of the coupling between a product set and the fixed diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intersection is the inverse image of a product set under the diagonal embedding, exposing intersection stability as a coupled constraint problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Coupling

children.title: Transversality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric regularity supporting stable intersections.

knowledge_statements.title: Transversality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative normal-cone transversality for locally convex set pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let closed sets \(A_n,B_n,A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) satisfy \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\). A uniform local normal-angle transversality regime at \(z\in A\cap B\) consists of numbers \(r>0\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(n_0\) such that \(A_n\) and \(B_n\) are locally convex on \(\mathbb{B}(z,r)\) for every \(n\geq n_0\), and whenever \(a\in A_n\cap\mathbb{B}(z,r)\), \(b\in B_n\cap\mathbb{B}(z,r)\), \(u\in N_{A_n}(a)\cap\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\), and \(v\in N_{B_n}(b)\cap\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\),
\[
\|u+v\|\geq\alpha.
\]
Under this regime, the pair is locally linearly regular near \(z\), with constants uniform for all sufficiently large \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near each limiting intersection point, uniform separation of opposing unit normals is a quantitative transversality regime yielding eventually uniform local linear regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(A_n,B_n,A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) are closed, with \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\).
For each point under consideration \(z\in A\cap B\), the sets \(A_n\) and \(B_n\) are eventually locally convex on a common ball about \(z\).
Nearby unit normals satisfy a common lower bound \(\|u+v\|\geq\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pairs \((A_n,B_n)\) are locally linearly regular near \(z\), uniformly for all sufficiently large \(n\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to a locally convex closed set
open Euclidean ball of radius r centered at z

children.title: Feasibility Loss
children.top_down_role: Disappearance of common feasible points under limiting operations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(A_n\to\{0\}\) and \(B_n\to\{0\}\), one has \(A_n\cap B_n=\varnothing\to\varnothing\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary failure of intersection continuity without a coupling qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In \(\mathbb{R}\), set \(A_n=\{0\}\) and \(B_n=\{1/n\}\). Then
\[
A_n\to\{0\},\qquad B_n\to\{0\},
\]
but \(A_n\cap B_n=\varnothing\) for every \(n\). Consequently,
\[
A_n\cap B_n\to\varnothing\neq\{0\}=\bigl(\lim_n A_n\bigr)\cap\bigl(\lim_n B_n\bigr).
\]
Thus separate set convergence does not prevent complete loss of feasibility; an intersection qualification is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two singleton sequences can converge to the same point while remaining disjoint, so their feasible intersections converge to the empty set.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Loss

children.title: Minkowski Sum Limits
children.top_down_role: Limiting behavior of Minkowski sums.

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski Sum Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact finite-dimensional continuity of Minkowski addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_n,B_n,A,B\) be nonempty compact subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^d\), all contained in a common compact set. If \(A_n\to A\) and \(B_n\to B\) in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense, then
\[
A_n+B_n\to A+B,
\qquad
A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minkowski sums of uniformly bounded compact sets converge when both summand sequences converge.
assumptions_latex: All sets lie in a common compact set, and \(A_n\to A\), \(B_n\to B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_n+B_n\to A+B\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minkowski sum of two sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an algebraic set operation and does not assert any convexity, closedness, or limiting property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sets \(A\) and \(B\) in the same vector space, their Minkowski sum is \[A+B:=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Minkowski sum of two sets in the same vector space consists of every vector obtained by adding one element of the first set to one element of the second.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\}

source_evidence.locator: Extended Real-Valued Functions / Support Functions / Lemma 2.2
