However, the supplied book locators do not establish that the stated convex hypotheses alone yield the asserted graphical-derivative identity; the precise twice-epi-differentiability or proto-differentiability theorem must be inspected.

children.title: Subdifferential Graph Convergence
children.top_down_role: Graph limits of subdifferential and normal-cone mappings, including identification and failure regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Epi-convergence of \(f_n\) to \(f\) is equivalent to graphical convergence of \(\partial f_n\) to \(\partial f\) together with one convergent value anchor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Attouch theorem with additive constants fixed by an anchor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sequence \(f_n\) epi-converges to \(f\) if and only if
\[\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\to\operatorname{gph}\partial f\]
in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense and there exist \((x_n,v_n)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) and \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) such that \((x_n,v_n)\to(x,v)\) and \(f_n(x_n)\to f(x)\). In particular, epi-convergence implies graphical convergence of the convex subdifferentials; the value condition is required for the converse because subdifferentials do not detect additive constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex epi-convergence yields subdifferential graph convergence; conversely, graph convergence plus one convergent function-value anchor yields epi-convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Subdifferential Graph Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem has the expected finite-dimensional Attouch form and the value anchor addresses additive constants, but no source is supplied to confirm this exact equivalence and anchor formulation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(f_n\to f\) uniformly, \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) converges to \(\{(x,v):|v-2x|\le1\}\), not to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\).

notation.meaning: Subdifferential, equal here to the derivative because each function is smooth.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit smooth oscillatory counterexample verified algebraically
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonconvex example showing that uniform or epi-convergence does not control subgradient graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Since \(\lvert f_n(x)-f(x)\rvert\le n^{-1}\), the functions converge uniformly, hence epi-converge, to \(f\). Nevertheless,
\[\partial f_n(x)=\{2x+\cos(nx)\},\qquad \partial f(x)=\{2x\}.\]
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), phase-adjusted sequences \(x_n\to x\) realize every cluster value in \(2x+[-1,1]\), and no other cluster values occur. Consequently,
\[\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\to\{(x,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2:|v-2x|\le1\}\ne\operatorname{gph}\partial f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing oscillations in function values can leave order-one gradient oscillations, so nonconvex epi-convergence alone does not imply subdifferential graph convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Subdifferential Graph Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit calculation is internally correct and the counterexample content kind is appropriate: the graph limit is the stated strip even though the functions converge uniformly. A standard-field rationale alone does not provide the requested inspectable citation for this nontrivial graph-limit claim.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex normal-cone mappings converge graphically: \(\operatorname{gph}N_{C_n}\to\operatorname{gph}N_C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional closed-convex specialization of Mosco and Attouch convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-convex normal-cone convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(n\), let \(N_{C_n}=\partial\delta_{C_n}\), and similarly let \(N_C=\partial\delta_C\). Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence of nonempty closed convex sets in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) is equivalent to epi-convergence of their indicators. Therefore
\[\operatorname{gph}N_{C_n}=\operatorname{gph}\partial\delta_{C_n}\longrightarrow\operatorname{gph}\partial\delta_C=\operatorname{gph}N_C.\]
Equivalently, every convergent sequence of normal pairs has a normal limiting pair, and every pair in \(\operatorname{gph}N_C\) admits approximating pairs from \(\operatorname{gph}N_{C_n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence of nonempty closed convex sets in finite dimensions entails graphical convergence of their convex normal-cone mappings.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Graph Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional closed-convex specialization is mathematically plausible and correctly placed as a theorem, but the passage from set convergence through indicator epi-convergence to normal-cone graph convergence needs a specific authoritative source locator.

children.title: Subdifferential Graph-Convergence Tests
children.top_down_role: Representation-based diagnostic families for graph convergence.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graphical convergence \(A_n\to A\) is equivalent to pointwise convergence \(J_{\lambda A_n}x\to J_{\lambda A}x\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\).

notation.meaning: Resolvent of a maximal monotone operator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: resolvent characterization of maximal-monotone graph convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional maximal-monotone resolvent criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the everywhere single-valued resolvents
\[J_{\lambda A_n}=(I+\lambda A_n)^{-1},\qquad J_{\lambda A}=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}.\]
Then
\[\operatorname{gph}A_n\to\operatorname{gph}A\]
in the Painlevé--Kuratowski sense if and only if \(J_{\lambda A_n}(z)\to J_{\lambda A}(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\). The test reconstructs a graph pair through \(x=J_{\lambda A}(z)\) and \(v=(z-x)/\lambda\), so the resolvent limit simultaneously controls primal and operator coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal monotone graphs converge exactly when their resolvents at one fixed positive parameter converge pointwise everywhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent-Based Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition has the correct role for a resolvent-based test and states the standard finite-dimensional maximal-monotone criterion. No inspectable source is supplied for the exact equivalence between Painleve--Kuratowski graph convergence and pointwise resolvent convergence at one fixed parameter.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functions \(f_n\) epi-converge to \(f\) exactly when \(e_\lambda f_n(x)\to e_\lambda f(x)\) for every \(x\) and every \(\lambda>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Moreau-envelope characterization of finite-dimensional convex epi-convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise envelope test for finite-dimensional convex epi-convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda>0\), define
\[e_\lambda f_n(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\{f_n(y)+\frac{\|x-y\|^2}{2\lambda}\right\},\]
and define \(e_\lambda f\) analogously. Then \(f_n\) epi-converges to \(f\) if and only if
\[e_\lambda f_n(x)\to e_\lambda f(x)\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and every \(\lambda>0\). Moreover, where the envelopes are differentiated,
\[\nabla e_\lambda f_n(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_n}(x)\bigr),\]
linking envelope tests to resolvent tests for \(\partial f_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex epi-convergence is equivalent to pointwise convergence of all Moreau envelopes, whose gradients also encode the proximal resolvents.
knowledge_statements.title: Moreau-Envelope Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Moreau-envelope test container and is internally consistent for proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions in finite dimensions. A specific source is still required to confirm the exact quantification over points and parameters.

children.title: Primal–Dual Graph Tests
children.top_down_role: Graph-convergence tests using paired primal and dual data.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal and dual subgradient graph tests are equivalent under the coordinate swap \((x,v)\mapsto(v,x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Fenchel subgradient inversion and induced graph correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex primal-dual graph inversion test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \((x,v)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\), Fenchel duality gives
\[v\in\partial f_n(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\partial f_n^*(v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_n(x)+f_n^*(v)=\langle x,v\rangle.\]
Consequently,
\[\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n^*=\{(v,x):(x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\}.\]
Thus graphical convergence of the primal subdifferentials is equivalent to graphical convergence of the dual subdifferentials after swapping coordinates, and candidate graph pairs may be checked on either side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex subgradient pair is simultaneously a dual subgradient pair, so primal and conjugate graph convergence tests coincide after swapping coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Graph Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Fenchel subgradient inversion gives the stated coordinate-swap correspondence, and duality is the correct content kind. The record nevertheless lacks an inspectable authoritative source locator supporting the graph-convergence test.

children.title: Conjugate-Function Tests
children.top_down_role: Graph-convergence tests expressed through convex conjugates.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One has \(f_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{epi}}f\) if and only if \(f_n^*\xrightarrow{\mathrm{epi}}f^*\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of a proper convex function.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional self-duality of convex epi-convergence under Fenchel conjugation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conjugacy test for convex epi-convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[f_n^*(v)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\{\langle v,x\rangle-f_n(x)\},\qquad f^*(v)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\{\langle v,x\rangle-f(x)\}.\]
Then Fenchel conjugation preserves and reflects convex epi-convergence:
\[f_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{epi}}f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_n^*\xrightarrow{\mathrm{epi}}f^*.\]
Hence convergence may be tested in either the primal or conjugate representation; applying conjugation twice returns the original proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For proper closed convex functions in finite dimensions, epi-convergence occurs precisely when the Fenchel conjugates epi-converge.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Function Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claim matches finite-dimensional self-duality of convex epi-convergence and the duality content kind fits the leaf. Because this is a convergence theorem rather than merely the definition of conjugation, a specific authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Duality-Gap Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics for mismatches between primal and dual convergence evidence.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Fenchel gap \(G_f(x,v)\) is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Fenchel--Young inequality and its equality characterization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Fenchel-gap certificate for convex subgradient graph membership; no quantitative or asymptotic distance-to-graph conclusion is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the Fenchel gap by
\[G_f(x,v)=f(x)+f^*(v)-\langle x,v\rangle.\]
The Fenchel--Young inequality gives \(G_f(x,v)\ge 0\), and
\[G_f(x,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v\in\partial f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\partial f^*(v).\]
Thus exact vanishing of the gap certifies that \((x,v)\) lies on the primal subdifferential graph and that \((v,x)\) lies on the dual subdifferential graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative Fenchel gap is zero exactly for primal-dual subgradient pairs, so exact zero certifies membership in both corresponding subdifferential graphs.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Diagnostics

children.title: Normalization Tests
children.top_down_role: Tests controlling additive or scale ambiguity across function families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single convergent value anchor fixes the additive drift left undetermined by subdifferential graph convergence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalization clause in the finite-dimensional Attouch convergence theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value anchoring removes additive indeterminacy in convex subdifferential limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A normalization test requires points \((x_n,v_n)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) and \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) such that
\[(x_n,v_n)\to(x,v),\qquad f_n(x_n)\to f(x).\]
Together with graphical convergence of \(\partial f_n\), this condition identifies \(f\) as the epi-limit. The value test is essential: replacing \(f_n\) by \(f_n+c_n\) leaves \(\partial f_n\) unchanged, while unconverged constants \(c_n\) can prevent convergence to the prescribed normalization of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subdifferential graphs ignore additive constants; convergence of one anchored function value fixes that drift and identifies the convex epi-limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed anchor condition correctly targets the additive indeterminacy invisible to subdifferentials, and condition is the correct content kind. Its sufficiency together with graphical convergence is the normalization clause of an Attouch-type theorem and requires a specific authoritative source locator.

children.title: Anchoring Tests
children.top_down_role: Tests using reference points or reference values to stabilize identification.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convergent triples \((x_n,x_n^*,f_n(x_n))\to(x,x^*,f(x))\) anchor the additive constants.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value anchoring for convex subdifferential graph convergence.

source_refs.locator: E. Pointwise and Graphical Convergence p. 166

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An anchoring test is satisfied when there exist \((x,x^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) and \((x_n,x_n^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) such that \(x_n\to x\), \(x_n^*\to x^*\), and \(f_n(x_n)\to f(x)\). Because subdifferential graphs are unchanged by additive constants, this value convergence supplies the normalization needed to identify the functional limit rather than merely its subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent graph point together with convergence of its function value fixes the additive normalization and identifies the limiting convex function.
knowledge_statements.title: Anchoring Tests

source_witnesses.locator: E. Pointwise and Graphical Convergence p. 166

children.title: Additive-Drift Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Detection of convergence ambiguity caused by uncontrolled additive constants.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graphical information alone cannot detect the drift \((c_n)\), since \(\partial(f_n+c_n)=\partial f_n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects the additive indeterminacy invisible to subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_n=f_n+c_n\). Then \(\partial g_n=\partial f_n\) for every \(n\), regardless of the behavior of \((c_n)\). Thus identical or graphically convergent subdifferentials do not imply convergence of the functions. For example, if \(f_n=f\) and \(c_n\to+\infty\), then \(\partial g_n=\partial f\), while \(g_n(x)\to+\infty\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). A normalization or anchoring value is therefore necessary to identify a particular functional representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding arbitrary constants leaves every subdifferential unchanged; divergent constants can destroy functional convergence while all subdifferential graphs remain identical.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Drift Diagnostics

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The common subdifferential graph identifies the function only modulo an additive constant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional nonidentifiability from an unanchored graphical limit.

source_refs.locator: E. Pointwise and Graphical Convergence p. 166

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since \(g=f+c\), one has \(\partial g(x)=\partial f(x)\) for every \(x\in H\), and hence \(\operatorname{gph}\partial g=\operatorname{gph}\partial f\). Consequently, a sequence whose subdifferential graphs converges to this common graph does not determine whether the corresponding functional representative is \(f\), \(g\), or another additive translate. Graphical convergence identifies the operator but requires an independent value normalization to identify a function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdifferential graph cannot distinguish two proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions differing by a constant, so an unanchored graph limit has no unique functional representative.
knowledge_statements.title: Graphical Limits Without Functional Identification

source_witnesses.locator: E. Pointwise and Graphical Convergence p. 166

children.title: Attouch Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Equivalence routes among convex variational convergence, subdifferential graphs, resolvents, envelopes, and dual representations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Variational Convergence for Functions and Operators
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Mosco convergence and convergence of subdifferentials
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Variational Convergence for Functions and Operators

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is \(\Gamma_0(H)\), whose members have maximal-monotone convex subdifferentials and well-defined proximal resolvents and Moreau envelopes for every positive parameter.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions from the Hilbert space to the extended reals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space convex regime for the Attouch theorem family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex lower-semicontinuous regime consists of functions \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) that are convex, lower semicontinuous in the norm topology, and proper, meaning that \(f(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in H\) and \(\operatorname{dom}f\neq\varnothing\). For \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), the convex subdifferential \(\partial f\) is maximal monotone, and the proximal resolvent and Moreau envelope are everywhere defined for every positive parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relevant regime is proper norm-lower-semicontinuous convex functions on a real Hilbert space, whose subdifferentials are maximal monotone and have everywhere-defined proximal resolvents and Moreau envelopes.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Lower-Semicontinuous Function Regimes

children.title: Mosco Convergence Route
children.top_down_role: Attouch-type stability organized through Mosco convergence of convex functions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mosco convergence combines a weak sequential lower bound with a strongly convergent recovery sequence.

notation.meaning: Weak convergence in the Hilbert space
Strong convergence in the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Hilbert-space definition of Mosco convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((f_n)\) Mosco-converges to \(f\) if both of the following conditions hold: for every sequence \((x_n)\subset H\) with \(x_n\rightharpoonup x\), one has \(f(x)\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n(x_n)\); and for every \(x\in H\), there exists a sequence \((x_n)\subset H\) with \(x_n\to x\) such that \(f(x)\geq\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_n(x_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mosco convergence means that every weakly convergent sequence satisfies the lower bound and every point admits a strongly convergent recovery sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Mosco Convergence Route

children.title: Subdifferential Graph Route
children.top_down_role: Attouch-type stability organized through graphical convergence of subdifferentials.

assumptions_latex: The graphs \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) converge graphically to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) in the topology specified by the applicable Attouch theorem.
There exist \((x_n,x_n^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) and \((x,x^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) such that \(x_n\to x\), \(x_n^*\to x^*\), and \(f_n(x_n)\to f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the precise Attouch graphical-convergence hypotheses, \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\).

notation.meaning: Graphical convergence of set-valued operators in the topology specified by the cited theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converse Attouch route with explicit additive anchoring; the exact graphical topology must follow the cited theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) converges graphically to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) in the topology required by the applicable Attouch theorem. If there exist \((x_n,x_n^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) and \((x,x^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) such that \(x_n\to x\), \(x_n^*\to x^*\), and \(f_n(x_n)\to f(x)\), then \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\). The value condition removes the additive ambiguity left by subdifferential data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the precise graphical-convergence topology in Attouch's theorem, convergence of convex subdifferentials yields Mosco convergence when one convergent graph point also carries a convergent function value.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Graph Route

children.title: Mosco–Graph Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes supporting equivalence between function convergence and subdifferential graph convergence.

assumptions_latex: Graphical convergence is interpreted in the topology specified by the applicable Attouch theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the precise Attouch hypotheses, \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\) is equivalent to anchored graphical convergence of \(\partial f_n\) to \(\partial f\).

notation.meaning: Graphical convergence in the topology specified by the cited theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attouch equivalence for proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, with the exact graphical topology fixed by the source theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the precise topology and hypotheses of the applicable Attouch theorem, \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\) holds if and only if \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) converges graphically to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) and there exist \((x_n,x_n^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f_n\) and \((x,x^*)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) such that \(x_n\to x\), \(x_n^*\to x^*\), and \(f_n(x_n)\to f(x)\). The anchoring clause removes the additive ambiguity in the reverse implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the precise topology and hypotheses of Attouch's theorem, Mosco convergence is equivalent to subdifferential graph convergence supplemented by one convergent value anchor.
knowledge_statements.title: Mosco–Graph Equivalence Regimes

children.title: Resolvent Convergence Route
children.top_down_role: Attouch-type convergence characterized through resolvent families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\), then \(J_\lambda^{f_n}x\to J_\lambda^f x\) strongly for every \(x\in H\).

notation.meaning: Proximal resolvent of the convex subdifferential
Identity operator on the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong pointwise convergence of proximal resolvents under Mosco convergence; any converse requires exact sourcing and additive anchoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\), then for every \(\lambda>0\) and every \(x\in H\), one has \[J_\lambda^{f_n}x=(I+\lambda\partial f_n)^{-1}x\to(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}x=J_\lambda^f x.\] Pointwise resolvent convergence identifies the limiting subdifferential but cannot distinguish additive translates of the functions. Therefore, a value anchor is required in any converse that concludes Mosco convergence to the specified representative \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mosco convergence gives strong pointwise convergence of every proximal resolvent; resolvent data alone cannot fix the additive normalization required by a converse to a specified function.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Convergence Route

children.title: Moreau-Envelope Convergence Route
children.top_down_role: Attouch-type convergence characterized through Moreau-envelope families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the precise Attouch characterization, Mosco convergence is equivalent to pointwise convergence of the Moreau envelopes for every positive parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau-envelope characterization retaining additive normalization; the one-parameter variant requires an exact theorem source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), define the Moreau envelope by \[e_\lambda f(x)=\inf_{y\in H}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert x-y\rVert^2\right\}.\] Under the standard Hilbert-space Attouch characterization, \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\) if and only if \(e_\lambda f_n(x)\to e_\lambda f(x)\) for every \(\lambda>0\) and every \(x\in H\). Whether convergence for one fixed positive parameter alone is sufficient must be stated only with the exact hypotheses of the cited theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the standard Hilbert-space characterization, Mosco convergence is equivalent to pointwise convergence of the Moreau envelopes for every positive parameter; a one-parameter variant requires exact sourcing.
knowledge_statements.title: Moreau-Envelope Convergence Route

children.title: Resolvent–Envelope Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Transfer of convergence information between resolvents and Moreau envelopes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal resolvent is recovered from the envelope gradient by \(J_\lambda^f=I-\lambda\nabla e_\lambda f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise identity connecting proximal mappings and envelope gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in H\), the minimizer in the Moreau-envelope formula is unique and equals \(J_\lambda^f x\). The envelope is Fréchet differentiable and satisfies \[\nabla e_\lambda f(x)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\bigl(x-J_\lambda^f x\bigr),\qquad J_\lambda^f x=x-\lambda\nabla e_\lambda f(x).\] Thus the resolvent and the envelope gradient determine each other pointwise, while envelope values additionally retain the additive normalization of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moreau-envelope gradient equals the scaled residual from the proximal point, so the resolvent and gradient determine each other.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent–Envelope Correspondence

children.title: Conjugacy Route
children.top_down_role: Attouch-type convergence transported through convex conjugation.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space identified with its continuous dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fenchel conjugation preserves and reflects Mosco convergence: \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\) if and only if \(f_n^*\xrightarrow{M}f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-duality of Mosco convergence under Fenchel conjugation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u\in H\), define the Fenchel conjugate by \[f^*(u)=\sup_{x\in H}\bigl\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\bigr\}.\] Then \(f_n\xrightarrow{M}f\) if and only if \(f_n^*\xrightarrow{M}f^*\). Hence a Mosco-convergence problem may be transferred to the conjugate sequence and returned by biconjugation, since every \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\) satisfies \(f^{**}=f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a Hilbert space identified with its dual, Fenchel conjugation preserves and reflects Mosco convergence, allowing convergence to be checked on the conjugate functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy Route

children.title: Duality Route
children.top_down_role: Attouch-type convergence analyzed through primal–dual representations.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space identified with its continuous dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conjugation reflects the subdifferential graph: \((x,u)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) if and only if \((u,x)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel duality expressed through inverse subdifferentials and graph reflection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,u\in H\), the following conditions are equivalent: \(u\in\partial f(x)\); \(x\in\partial f^*(u)\); and \[f(x)+f^*(u)=\langle u,x\rangle.\] Consequently, \(\partial f^*=(\partial f)^{-1}\), and the graph of \(\partial f^*\) is obtained from the graph of \(\partial f\) by interchanging the primal and dual coordinates. This reflection transfers graphical-convergence statements between the primal and conjugate subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel equality characterizes mutually dual subgradients, making the conjugate subdifferential the inverse of the primal subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality Route

children.title: Biconjugate Closure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Closure regimes affecting recovery across conjugate representations.

assumptions_latex: d4b3 is a Banach space with continuous dual \(X^*\).
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and admits a continuous affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f^{**}=\operatorname{cl}_{\|\cdot\|}\!\operatorname{conv}f,\qquad f=f^{**}\iff f\text{ is lower semicontinuous and convex}.\]

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate and biconjugate with respect to the pairing between the Banach space and its continuous dual.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Fenchel–Moreau closure identity under a continuous affine-minorant hypothesis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel–Moreau closure on a Banach space; no topology-dependent Attouch extension is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f^*(x^*)=\sup_{x\in X}\{\langle x^*,x\rangle-f(x)\}\) and \(f^{**}(x)=\sup_{x^*\in X^*}\{\langle x^*,x\rangle-f^*(x^*)\}\). Then the biconjugate is the greatest norm-lower-semicontinuous convex function majorized by \(f\), namely \(f^{**}=\operatorname{cl}_{\|\cdot\|}\operatorname{conv}f\). Consequently, the biconjugation step closes a conjugacy argument without altering the target precisely when \(f\) is lower semicontinuous and convex; for every proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(f\), one has \(f=f^{**}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Biconjugation produces the lower-semicontinuous convex closure; it leaves a proper function unchanged exactly in the lower-semicontinuous convex regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Biconjugate Closure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assumption begins with the corrupted token “d4b3” instead of defining X. The topology-sensitive Banach-space biconjugate closure identity also needs an inspectable authoritative locator before its precise formulation can be relied upon.

children.title: Normalization Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdown of equivalence caused by absent or inconsistent normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of a proper epigraphical limit when additive constants are not normalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(n\), addition of the constant \(n\) gives \(\partial f_n(x)=\partial q(x)=\{x\}\) at each \(x\in X\). Thus the subdifferential graphs are identical and converge trivially. Nevertheless, for every sequence \(x_n\to x\), one has \(f_n(x_n)=\tfrac12\|x_n\|^2+n\to+\infty\). Hence \(f_n\) epigraphically converges only to the improper function identically equal to \(+\infty\), demonstrating that operator convergence cannot recover a proper potential without normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical subdifferentials can accompany potentials drifting to positive infinity, so operator convergence alone does not yield a proper epigraphical limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f_n=\partial q\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad \operatorname*{e\!\!-lim}_{n\to\infty}f_n\equiv +\infty.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct computation using invariance of subgradients under additive constants

children.title: Additive-Drift Regimes
children.top_down_role: Function sequences differing through uncontrolled additive constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Drift Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of constant vertical drift for a fixed proper convex potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every real constant \(c_n\), vertical translation leaves the subdifferential unchanged: \(\partial(f+c_n)=\partial f\). If \(c_n\to c\in\mathbb R\), then \(f_n\) epigraphically converges to \(f+c\). If \(c_n\to+\infty\), its epigraphical limit is the improper function identically \(+\infty\). If \((c_n)\) has two distinct finite cluster values, the corresponding subsequences have different epigraphical limits, so the full sequence has no epigraphical limit although all subdifferential graphs coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive constants are invisible to subdifferentials but determine whether potentials converge, diverge to infinity, or have incompatible subsequential epigraphical limits.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f_n=\partial f,\qquad c_n\to c\Longrightarrow f_n\xrightarrow{e}f+c,\qquad c_n\to+\infty\Longrightarrow f_n\xrightarrow{e}+\infty.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive constants preserve subdifferentials and translate epigraphs vertically

children.title: Converse Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where operator-side or regularization-side convergence does not recover the expected function limit.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial f_n=\partial q\text{ for all }n,\qquad (f_n)\text{ has no epigraphical limit}.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: even and odd subsequences are constant sequences with distinct epigraphical limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the unnormalized converse from graphical subdifferential convergence to epigraphical convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(n\) and \(x\in X\), one has \(\partial f_n(x)=\{x\}=\partial q(x)\); hence the subdifferential graphs converge to \(\operatorname{gph}\partial q\). The even subsequence is constantly \(q+1\), whereas the odd subsequence is constantly \(q-1\). These subsequences have distinct epigraphical limits. Therefore \((f_n)\) has no epigraphical limit, showing that graphical convergence of subdifferentials does not imply epigraphical convergence of potentials unless additive constants are anchored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence may have a fixed subdifferential graph while alternating between two distinct vertical translates, invalidating an unnormalized Attouch converse.
knowledge_statements.title: Converse Failures

children.title: Anchoring Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Failure of reference-value information to identify a unique variational limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Anchoring Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An anchor controls normalization only when it remains compatible with the limiting local geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each \(f_n\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex and has the normalized minimizer \(a_n=n\), satisfying \(f_n(a_n)=0\) and \(0\in\partial f_n(a_n)\). However, the anchors escape every bounded subset of \(X\). For every convergent sequence \(x_n\to x\), the sequence \((x_n)\) is bounded and \((x_n-n)^2\to+\infty\). Thus \(f_n\) epigraphically converges to the improper function identically \(+\infty\); normalization at escaping points does not anchor a proper local limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-valued stationary anchors may escape to infinity, leaving every bounded region with an improper infinite epigraphical limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f_n(a_n)=0,\quad 0\in\partial f_n(a_n),\qquad a_n\to+\infty,\quad f_n\xrightarrow{e}+\infty.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct evaluation along bounded sequences and at the escaping minimizers

children.title: Graphical Limits of Implicit Solution Maps

knowledge_statements.title: Graphical Limits of Implicit Solution Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential graphical convergence in metric parameter and solution spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The outer limit of \(\operatorname{gph}S_n\) consists of all \((p,x)\in P\times X\) for which some subsequence \(n_k\) and points \((p_k,x_k)\in\operatorname{gph}S_{n_k}\) satisfy \((p_k,x_k)\to(p,x)\). The inner limit consists of all \((p,x)\in P\times X\) for which there exist \((p_n,x_n)\in\operatorname{gph}S_n\) eventually satisfying \((p_n,x_n)\to(p,x)\). The maps converge graphically to \(S\) precisely when \(\operatorname*{Liminf}_n\operatorname{gph}S_n=\operatorname*{Limsup}_n\operatorname{gph}S_n=\operatorname{gph}S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graphical convergence requires equality of the inner and outer limits of the solution-map graphs; sequentially, all limit solutions persist and no spurious ones appear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{gph}S_n=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{gph}S_n=\operatorname{gph}S.\]

source_refs.locator: A. Inner and Outer Limits p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each parameter \(p\in P\), the solution set of the variational system \(0\in F_n(p,x)\) is \(S_n(p)=\{x\in X:0\in F_n(p,x)\}\). Equivalently, its graph is the zero-level slice \(\operatorname{gph}S_n=\{(p,x)\in P\times X:(p,x,0)\in\operatorname{gph}F_n\}\). Consequently, limits of solution sets are limits of these slices; convergence of the entire residual graphs alone need not ensure convergence of their zero-level slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit solution map is the zero-level slice of a residual graph, so solution-set convergence concerns limits of those particular slices.

children.title: Solution-Loss Regimes
children.top_down_role: Limits in which approximating solution families lose feasible or solution points.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Loss Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of all solutions through escape to infinity in a noncompact ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every approximating solution set \(S_n=\{n\}\) is nonempty. Any selection \(x_n\in S_n\) satisfies \(x_n=n\) and therefore has no convergent subsequence in \(X\). Hence no point belongs to the outer sequential limit, and \(\operatorname*{Limsup}_n S_n=\varnothing\). The inner limit is also empty. Thus nonemptiness of every approximating solution set does not preserve a solution in the limit without compactness or local boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonempty solution sets can escape to infinity, leaving both their inner and outer limits empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S_n\ne\varnothing\text{ for all }n,\quad \operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}S_n=\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}S_n=\varnothing.\]

notation.meaning: Outer and inner sequential set limits.

children.title: Solution-Branching Regimes
children.top_down_role: Limits involving splitting, merging, or proliferation of solution branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Branching Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two approximating solution branches coalesce into one limiting solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residuals \(F_n\) converge uniformly on bounded subsets of \(\mathbb R\) to \(F\). For every \(n\), the equation \(F_n(x)=0\) has the two solutions \(-n^{-1/2}\) and \(n^{-1/2}\), whereas the limiting equation \(F(x)=0\) has the single solution \(0\). Both branches converge to \(0\), so \(S_n\) converges to \(S=\{0\}\) while the local number of solution branches is not preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct solution branches may merge into one limiting solution even under locally uniform convergence of scalar residuals.

source_refs.locator: A. Inner and Outer Limits p. 109

children.title: Solution-Limit Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Disagreement between limits of solution sets and solutions of the limit system.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Limit Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual convergence without metric regularity need not imply convergence of zero sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each bounded set \(B\subset\mathbb R\), one has \(\sup_{x\in B}|F_n(x)-F(x)|=n^{-1}\sup_{x\in B}|x|\to0\). Nevertheless, \(S_n=\{0\}\) for every \(n\), while every real number solves the limiting equation and hence \(S=\mathbb R\). Therefore the set limit of \((S_n)\) is \(\{0\}\), strictly smaller than the solution set of the limiting residual. The zero-set operation is not continuous without a regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally uniform residual convergence can miss most limiting solutions when the limiting equation loses regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_n\to F\text{ uniformly on bounded sets},\quad \lim_{n\to\infty}S_n=\{0\}\ne\mathbb R=S.\]

source_refs.locator: A. Inner and Outer Limits p. 109

children.title: Outer–Inner Limit Gaps
children.top_down_role: Asymmetry between outer and inner limits of solution mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer–Inner Limit Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical alternating sequence with distinct outer and inner solution-set limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The even subsequence converges as sets to \(\{0\}\), and the odd subsequence converges as sets to \(\{1\}\). Thus both \(0\) and \(1\) are attainable subsequential limits, giving \(\operatorname*{Limsup}_n S_n=\{0,1\}\). No single sequence \(x_n\in S_n\) converges, because it alternates between \(0\) and \(1\); hence \(\operatorname*{Liminf}_n S_n=\varnothing\). The strict gap shows that the solution sets possess no Painlev–Kuratowski limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating singleton solution sets have outer limit containing both cluster points but empty inner limit, so no set limit exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{Liminf}_{n\to\infty}S_n=\varnothing\subsetneq\{0,1\}=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{n\to\infty}S_n.\]

notation.meaning: Outer and inner sequential set limits.

children.top_down_role: The convergence-theoretic role of relaxation and approximation; detailed envelope, microstructure, and integral-representation theories are assigned to calculus-of-variations chapters.
